Rocket Lab.role: Small-launch provider and space systems maker expanding into satellite components and constellations; the 'space compute' angle is early and speculative, and the pre-profit, capital-intensive model with lumpy government/commercial demand places it in high-beta disruptive territory.

Nvidia peer / Intel.role: Legacy x86 CPU leader and aspiring foundry player attempting a costly turnaround; sits in AI-infra but with weak AI positioning, cyclical earnings, eroding share, and heavy capital intensity making the recovery thesis uncertain.

Alphabet peer / n/a skip.role: GlobalFoundries is a specialty foundry serving automotive, IoT, and defense on mature/differentiated nodes rather than leading-edge AI logic; it sits as cyclical AI-infra with modest growth, moderate moat, and meaningful capex sensitivity given no leading-edge or hyperscaler AI exposure.

GlobalFoundries.role: GlobalFoundries is a specialty foundry focused on differentiated non-leading-edge nodes (RF, power, automotive, IoT) rather than bleeding-edge AI logic, giving it stable but cyclical end-market exposure with limited direct AI-compute upside and modest moat versus TSMC.

United Microelectronics.role: UMC is a Taiwanese pure-play foundry focused on mature and specialty process nodes (28nm and above), serving consumer, automotive and IoT chips rather than leading-edge AI logic; it sits as a cyclical, moderate-moat AI-infra name with limited direct AI leverage and exposure to broad semiconductor de

STMicroelectronics.role: Broad-based analog, MCU, power and MEMS supplier levered to automotive and industrial end-markets; sits as a cyclical defensive name given its diversified franchise but ongoing inventory correction and weak near-term revenue growth.

NXP Semiconductors.role: NXP is a leading automotive and industrial semiconductor supplier whose edge processors, microcontrollers and radar chips increasingly embed AI at the vehicle level; it sits in AI-infra with moderate growth given cyclical auto exposure and a slow-recovering revenue base (rev YoY ~4.5%), but with dur

ON Semiconductor.role: Leading supplier of power management and image-sensing chips for autos and industrial markets; sits as a cyclical AI-infra adjacency with modest near-term growth given flat YoY revenue and heavy exposure to auto/industrial capex cycles.

Analog Devices.role: ADI is a leading high-performance analog and mixed-signal semiconductor maker whose power, data-conversion and signal chips increasingly feed AI data-center and networking builds; broad diversification and a strong moat make it durable but cyclical exposure across industrial/auto tempers its AI-pure

Skyworks Solutions.role: Skyworks supplies RF front-end modules for smartphones and IoT; heavy Apple concentration and flat/declining revenue make it a cyclical, mobile-tethered name with modest AI-edge exposure rather than a data-center growth story.

Qorvo.role: Qorvo makes RF front-end and power semiconductors heavily tied to the smartphone cycle (notably Apple), a mature, competitive, and cyclical business with limited direct AI leverage, placing it as a mid-quality cyclical semiconductor name.

Allegro MicroSystems.role: Allegro makes magnetic (Hall-effect) and current sensor ICs concentrated in automotive/EV and industrial applications; its cyclical, auto-levered demand and modest single-digit growth make it a volatile mid-cap with a solid but narrow niche moat rather than a core AI beneficiary.

Power Integrations.role: Fabless supplier of high-voltage power conversion chips for appliances, industrial, and increasingly data-center/EV power, with modest AI-adjacent exposure; flat recent revenue and cyclical end-markets keep it a mid-quality, moderately cyclical name rather than a core AI-infra play.

Diodes Incorporated.role: Diodes makes commodity discrete and analog power semiconductors for broad industrial, consumer, automotive and computing markets; modest AI exposure, cyclical earnings, and a fragmented, low-moat position place it as a mid-tier cyclical AI-infra peripheral.

Cirrus Logic.role: Designs mixed-signal audio and haptic/power ICs heavily concentrated in Apple smartphones; modest growth and customer concentration risk place it as a cyclical, mature semiconductor name with limited direct AI exposure.

Synaptics.role: Synaptics designs human-interface, connectivity, and edge-AI processors for IoT, PC, and consumer devices; modest single-digit growth, mid-tier moat, and cyclical consumer/IoT end-markets place it as a mid-quality edge-AI play with meaningful sensitivity to demand swings.

Cadence Design Systems.role: Cadence is a duopoly EDA vendor whose recurring software/IP licenses are essential to all advanced chip design, giving durable, non-discretionary demand tied to secular semiconductor complexity growth.

Synopsys.role: Dominant EDA vendor supplying the design software and IP essential for advanced AI/semiconductor chip development; recurring, mission-critical revenue with a durable duopoly moat alongside Cadence, placing it near defensive-quality infrastructure.

Ansys.role: Leading engineering simulation software vendor with sticky, recurring-license revenue across aerospace, semiconductors and industrials; sits defensive given high moat and durable subscription earnings, with modest growth pending the Synopsys acquisition.

Entegris.role: Entegris supplies high-purity materials, filtration, and advanced deposition chemistries consumed in semiconductor fabrication; its consumable-heavy, wafer-start-driven revenue gives moderate cyclicality with a durable moat, placing it in mid-quality AI-infra.

MKS Instruments.role: MKS supplies critical subsystems (vacuum, plasma, lasers, photonics) and materials for semiconductor fab equipment; it benefits from AI-driven capex but sits mid-supply-chain with cyclical WFE exposure and a leveraged balance sheet from the Atotech deal, so it is durable but not immune to downturns.

Brooks / Azenta.role: Azenta provides sample storage, cryogenic automation, and life-sciences lab tooling plus a legacy semiconductor automation segment; modest ~3% growth, mixed margins, and cyclical capital-equipment exposure place it as a mid-quality diversified name with only tangential AI/semiconductor leverage.

FormFactor.role: FormFactor is the leading maker of probe cards and test/measurement systems for semiconductor wafer testing, benefiting from HBM/AI chip complexity but exposed to cyclical semi capex and test spending swings.

Photronics.role: Leading independent photomask maker supplying critical masks to chip and display foundries; sits as a cyclical, moderately-moated infra supplier with flat recent revenue and modest exposure to secular chip growth.

Cohu.role: Cohu supplies test handlers, contactors, and consumables for semiconductor back-end test; a niche leader tied to cyclical chip capex and unit volumes, hence moderate moat and cyclical earnings.

Amkor Technology.role: Amkor is the largest US-based outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) provider, benefiting from advanced packaging demand tied to AI, but sits mid-tier given cyclical end markets, thin margins, and competition from ASE and JCET.

Vishay Intertechnology.role: Vishay is a broad-line maker of discrete semiconductors and passive components (resistors, capacitors, inductors) serving industrial, auto, and some AI/data-center power designs; it sits as a cyclical component supplier with modest growth, fragmented competition, and demand tied to end-market capex

Littelfuse.role: Diversified maker of circuit protection, power semiconductors and sensors with some AI/data-center exposure; cyclical industrial/auto end-markets and modest growth make it a moderate-beta, semi-durable name rather than a pure AI play.

Jabil.role: Diversified electronics manufacturing services provider capturing AI/data-center hardware assembly demand, but as a low-margin, cyclical, thin-moat contract manufacturer it sits mid-quality with capex-sensitive earnings.

Flex.role: Diversified EMS/ODM provider whose data-center power, cooling, and rack integration segment (via Anord Mardix and cloud/AI infrastructure builds) benefits from hyperscaler capex, but thin margins, cyclical exposure, and a fragmented, competitive manufacturing market cap its moat and durability.

Sanmina.role: Diversified EMS/contract manufacturer with growing exposure to AI server and data-center hardware assembly; thin-margin, cyclical build business with modest moat, so it sits as a mid-quality AI-infra name.

Belden.role: Belden supplies signal transmission cabling and connectivity solutions with growing data-center exposure, but remains a cyclical, industrially-tied hardware vendor with modest single-digit growth and only partial AI leverage.

Pure peer / NetApp.role: NetApp is a mature enterprise storage vendor pivoting toward AI/flash and cloud data services; its flat-to-slightly-negative TTM revenue and modest forward multiple place it as a defensive, moderately durable name with real but not dominant AI-storage exposure.

Digital Realty Trust.role: Owns and operates global data center real estate leased to hyperscalers and enterprises; recurring lease revenue and AI-driven demand support durability, but capital intensity and rate sensitivity temper growth and valuation.

Equinix.role: Leading global colocation and interconnection REIT whose recurring, contracted revenue and neutral peering ecosystem make it durable AI-adjacent infrastructure rather than a cyclical capex play.

Iron Mountain.role: Records-storage REIT expanding into data center colocation; its legacy storage business is recurring and non-discretionary, while the data center segment is a smaller but faster-growing AI-adjacent driver, warranting a defensive classification with modest growth.

GE Vernova.role: GE Vernova supplies gas turbines, grid equipment, and electrification hardware benefiting from AI datacenter power demand; it sits in AI-infra as a picks-and-shovels beneficiary, but its exposure is partly cyclical utility/energy capex rather than pure secular AI spend.

Eaton.role: Diversified electrical equipment maker supplying power distribution, switchgear and backup systems for data centers; AI buildout drives its Electrical Americas segment but broad industrial exposure tempers both upside and downside.

Emerson Electric.role: Emerson is a diversified process/industrial automation supplier whose control and power management systems support data-center and factory electrification, but only a fraction of revenue is AI-relevant and demand is tied to cyclical industrial capex, placing it in the defensive group with moderate d

Hubbell.role: Hubbell makes utility-grade electrical and grid components benefiting from data-center power buildout and grid modernization; it sits as a durable, moderately cyclical infrastructure supplier with steady but modest growth rather than a hyper-growth AI name.

Schneider peer / Powell.role: Powell makes custom electrical distribution and control equipment (switchgear, bus duct) for utility, oil/gas, and increasingly data-center power infrastructure; project-based backlog gives near-term visibility but demand is cyclical and tied to capex budgets, placing it as a peripheral AI-infra ben

Vertiv peer / Modine.role: Diversified thermal management supplier whose fast-growing data center cooling segment rides AI capex, but legacy HVAC/automotive exposure and cyclical, capex-linked demand temper the AI premium.

Johnson Controls.role: Diversified building-controls and HVAC vendor whose data-center thermal-management segment rides AI capex; solid but cyclical exposure with modest overall growth keeps it mid-quality AI-infra.

MDU peer / EMCOR.role: EMCOR is a diversified mechanical/electrical construction and facilities-services contractor benefiting from data-center buildout demand; it sits in AI-infra with moderate quality but cyclical, project-based earnings exposed to construction capex swings.

Curtiss-Wright.role: Diversified industrial supplying flow control, valves, and instrumentation to naval/commercial nuclear, defense, and aerospace; nuclear segment is a durable but modest slice of a slow-growing, regulated market, giving stable but non-hyper-growth earnings.

BWX Technologies.role: Sole-source manufacturer of naval nuclear reactors for the US Navy with growing medical isotope and commercial SMR exposure; durable government-anchored backlog gives defensive, low-beta characteristics despite modest growth.

Oklo.role: Pre-revenue developer of small modular fast reactors targeting AI/data-center power demand, with no deployed plants or commercial revenue yet, making it a highly speculative, execution- and regulatory-dependent bet.

GE Aerospace peer / Twilio.role: Twilio is a cloud communications (CPaaS) platform layering AI messaging/voice tools onto its usage-based API business; modest ~6-8% growth, decent recurring revenue but competitive pressure and usage cyclicality cap its moat and durability.

MongoDB.role: Document-oriented NoSQL database (Atlas cloud) positioned as a backend for AI-native applications; recurring consumption revenue gives durability, but growth has decelerated sharply and it faces stiff competition from hyperscaler-native databases, limiting moat and TAM capture.

Salesforce.role: Salesforce is the leading enterprise CRM/SaaS platform layering Agentforce AI agents onto a large recurring subscription base; durable and sticky but growth has slowed to low-single digits and AI monetization remains early, so it sits as a quality mid-cap platform rather than a hyper-growth AI name.

Adobe.role: Adobe is a dominant subscription-based creative and document software leader integrating generative AI (Firefly) into its suite; recurring revenue and a wide moat make it durable, but decelerating ~3% YoY growth and AI-driven competitive pressure temper its upside.

ARKK (ARK Innovation).role: disruptive-innovation basket LED BY TESLA (~10%), then AMD, CRISPR, Tempus AI, Robinhood. High beta, rich multiples, Tesla-driven idiosyncratic swings — NOT a semis basket.

QQQ (Nasdaq-100).role: Nasdaq-100 mega-cap tech; quality, but rich and tech-tilted.

VOO (S&P 500).role: broad US large-cap; the market itself — durable, diversified.

SCHD (Dividend).role: quality-dividend value basket; low beta, cheap, durable earnings.

DTCR (Data Ctr Infra).role: data-center REITs & digital infra (Equinix, Digital Realty, American Tower); physical, contracted, durable — low beta.

GRID (Smart Grid).role: grid/power equipment for the AI electricity demand (Eaton, Quanta, GE Vernova); inelastic infra spend.

NUKE (Nuclear/Uranium).role: nuclear/uranium for data-center baseload (Constellation, Vistra, Cameco, BWX); high-growth but cyclical/volatile.

VGT (Info Tech).role: broad US information-technology sector; mega-cap heavy, durable.

IGV (Software).role: application & infrastructure software basket; higher multiple, subscription-durable.
